strategy.summary: GET /products filters the in-memory catalogue (120 products) by a case-insensitive name substring `q`, returns one page selected by `limit` (default 20, capped at MAX_LIMIT) and `offset`, with `total` = number of matches, and refuses non-whole limit/offset or limit < 1 with 400. Integration tests start the real app in-process on port 0 and call the endpoint over HTTP.
inScope: GET /products query parameters q, limit, offset
outOfScope: GET /products/:id and POST /orders (not part of this ticket)
assumptions: The limit cap is 50 (MAX_LIMIT in src/app.js), not the README's 100; asked as Q1, earlier runs were told the README is stale. Tests import MAX_LIMIT and DEFAULT_LIMIT from src/app.js.
The real app runs in-process (createApp on port 0); nothing is faked. The catalogue is the fixed PRODUCTS list from src/catalogue.js, which GET /products never changes.
Server start/stop moves into a shared helper test/helpers/server.js used by both test/products.test.js and the new spec.
openQuestions: README says limit goes up to 100 while code caps at 50 (Q1); README should be corrected.

acceptanceCriteria.text: q matches products whose name contains it, in any case; without q every product is listed.
Results come a page at a time with limit and offset, the response gives the total number of matches, and large limits are capped at MAX_LIMIT (50).
A limit or offset that isn't a whole number, or a limit below 1, is refused with 400.

review.standard: Test case design standards: base each case on what the code does / a case listed on a criterion must fail when the criterion isn't met (AC1 'name contains q'; strategy TC1 'mixed-case q matching mid-name')
review.summary: The substring search test uses q=TeA, which only ever matches at the start of a name ('Teapot n', 'Tea strainer n'), so no test in the suite checks a match in the middle of a name.
review.failureScenario: Say listProducts in src/app.js:23 is changed to `p.name.toLowerCase().startsWith(q)`, so search only matches the start of a name. TC1 still gets total 30 with 'Teapot 1' and 'Tea strainer 1'. TC5 (q=kettle, line 57) still gets 15 because 'Kettle' is also at the start. TC2 (q=zzz) still gets 0. Every test passes even though AC1's 'contains' behaviour is broken, which is the prefix-only risk the strategy says TC1 covers. Fix: use a mixed-case term that appears only mid-name, e.g. q='StRaInEr' (total 15, every item is 'Tea strainer n') or q='GRIND' (15 Coffee grinders).

questions.question: README.md says GET /products `limit` goes "up to 100", but src/app.js caps it at MAX_LIMIT = 50. Which cap should the tests hold the API to? (Earlier runs on this ticket were told 50, and that the README is out of date.)
questions.assumption: The cap is 50, as the code says. Tests import MAX_LIMIT from src/app.js, and the README is stale (I'll suggest a README fix as a follow-up).
questions.answer: The cap is 50, as the code does. The README is out of date; leave it as it is and test against 50.
